text: The game screen is longer than the visible area on phones (about 838px of content at 390px wide against about 660px visible), so it scrolls during play. The owner chose to accept this scroll on 2026-11-17 and gave no reason. Two alternatives were offered and not chosen. One was a shorter phone layout, which changes the reference design in misc/Quarto.html (that design draws the phone as a 390x844 frame with no browser bars). The other was a board that scales to the viewport height, which makes the squares smaller than the 44px touch size. Do not treat this scroll as a bug.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Rule choices made by the project owner, with the options that were turned down. (1) A player must call Quarto; the page does not detect a win by itself. Automatic detection was offered as the simpler option and was refused, because the owner wants the official rule where a player can miss a line. (2) A wrong call has no penalty. 'A wrong call loses' and 'one free wrong call per game' were offered and refused; the owner accepts that a player can press the button after each move, as in the physical game. (3) Undo removes only the player's own last action, until the opponent acts. 'Any player at any time' and 'the opponent must approve' were refused. The owner knows and accepts that this lets a player who gave a piece and then sees their own missed line undo and call it, if the opponent has not acted yet. Do not 'fix' this as a loophole. (4) No 2x2 square variant.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The designer's reference design is misc/Quarto.html, and the page is built from it. The file is a packed export: the root page holds a JSON manifest (base64, gzip) of 38 nested pages, and each nested page is again a manifest plus a template; unpack both levels to read the frames. The page differs from the frames in these places ON PURPOSE; do not 'correct' the page to match them. (1) While the page is not connected, every game control is off, 'New game' included; the frames leave 'New game' on. The owner decided that play stops when the connection is lost. (2) 'Undo' is on during the opponent's turn when the last action is the player's own; the 'opponent's turn' frame shows it off, which is against the rules the owner chose. In general the rules in game.js decide which control is on, and the design gives only the look. (3) The design gives no time for when a short connection loss becomes the 'Connection lost' notice; the owner accepted about 5 seconds. Font history: the first design used Figtree, which has no Greek letters; players type names in Greek, so the designer and the owner replaced it fully with Commissioner. The Cyrillic and Vietnamese subsets that the design file also contains were left out on purpose. Wording: the owner chose the designer's wording over the first version's strings; strings for states that have no frame were written to match it.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Firefox showed 'Connection lost' for about 30 seconds after each connect, because Firefox fetch resolves only at the first body byte and Gweet sent nothing until its 30-second keepalive. The owner fixed this in Gweet (commit ff06d79 in skorokithakis/gweet): the stream now sends one keepalive newline as soon as the subscription is registered, to ALL clients. Rejected: (1) an opt-in query parameter for the early newline, which would protect existing Gweet clients that read only the first line or treat any byte as a message; the owner accepted that risk. (2) A Quarto-only fix that shows 'Connected' before the stream response arrives, because it can show 'Connected' while no updates arrive, against the rule that play stops when the connection is lost. (3) A longer 'Connection lost' delay, because it hides the symptom.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The project owner chose online play through Gweet (their own HTTP message queue, server https://gweet.stavros.io) over two other options: play on one shared device, and peer-to-peer WebRTC. Play on one shared device is an explicit non-goal, not an oversight. Protection against cheating is also an explicit non-goal: any person with the room link can write any state, and the owner accepts this for games between friends. When two players act at the same moment, last write wins and one action is lost; the owner accepted this in place of a fair tie-break.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>
